quickAnswer: Washington public school calendars are set by local districts, so first day, last day, winter break, mid-winter break, spring break, conference days, TRI or staff days, weekly early release, and emergency closure makeup days vary by district. Reviewed Washington pages on MySchoolDates include Seattle Public Schools, Lake Washington School District, and Northshore School District.
about:
Washington public school calendars are approved locally by district. Large districts often begin in late August or early September and end in June, but start dates, conference days, weekly early-release schedules, staff-only dates, and emergency closure plans can differ even within the same metro area.

Reviewed Puget Sound district pages on MySchoolDates include Seattle Public Schools, Lake Washington School District, and Northshore School District. SPS separates student attendance dates from TRI staff days, semester and grading periods, conferences, and emergency makeup days. LWSD highlights kindergarten family connections, LEAP days, preschool and SNAPS dates, and closure make-up days. NSD highlights weekly early release, elementary-only conference dismissals, teacher grading/non-student days, commencements, and emergency make-up days.

Families should treat the districtwide calendar as the starting point, then check the school calendar for bell schedules, transportation notices, testing, athletics, performances, graduation details, and campus-specific events. Weather and emergency closures can also change the end of the school year or activate makeup days.

faqs.q: When do Washington schools usually start?
faqs.a: Washington school start dates vary by district. Many districts begin in late August or early September, but families should select their district calendar to confirm the official first day.

faqs.q: Are Washington school calendars the same statewide?
faqs.a: No. Washington school calendars are approved locally by district, so start dates, breaks, conference days, TRI days, and makeup-day rules can differ.

faqs.q: What are TRI days on Washington school calendars?
faqs.a: TRI days are staff work or training days listed by some districts, including Seattle Public Schools. Other Washington districts may use different labels, such as LEAP, teacher grading, or non-student days. They are not regular student attendance days unless the district says otherwise.

faqs.q: Do Washington schools have mid-winter break?
faqs.a: Many large Washington districts schedule a mid-winter break in February, often around Presidents Day, but the exact dates vary by district.

faqs.q: Can emergency closures change Washington school calendars?
faqs.a: Yes. District calendars may include emergency closure makeup days that can extend or alter the school year if snow, weather, or other closures occur.

faqs.q: Which Washington district calendars are reviewed on MySchoolDates?
faqs.a: Featured Washington pages include Seattle Public Schools, Lake Washington School District, and Northshore School District. Each page links official sources, PDFs, and a one-time calendar download when available.

faqs.q: Can I add a Washington school calendar to Google Calendar?
faqs.a: Yes. District pages on MySchoolDates include calendar download options when available, including ICS files that can be imported into Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, or Outlook.
